children: New Delhi, Oct. 25 -- KEC International shares will be in focus on Monday, 26 October, after the RPG Group company secured turnkey orders worth Rs.2,872 crore from Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd (PGCIL) for the design, supply and installation of 765 kV transmission lines.

The latest wins include the largest-ever order for KEC International's India transmission and distribution (T&D) business, strengthening its order book and reinforcing its presence in India's power transmission infrastructure segment.

According to the company, the projects are associated with the evacuation of 8.5 GW of renewable energy from Gujarat. The orders come amid rising electricity demand and continued investment in strengthening India's transmission network.

Vimal Kejriwal, Managing Director and CEO of KEC International, said the PGCIL wins reflected strong momentum in the company's T&D business. He added that the projects had substantially expanded its domestic T&D order book.
With these orders, KEC International's year-to-date order intake has crossed Rs.13,500 crore, including approximately Rs.9,500 crore from the T&D business.

The latest announcement follows another order win disclosed by the company on 23 October, when KEC International secured fresh orders worth Rs.1,006 crore across its T&D, civil, and cables-and-conductors businesses.
In its T&D business, the company won an order for a 400 kV transmission line project in Oman, along with orders to supply towers, hardware, and poles in the Americas.

Its civil business secured a repeat order from a prominent healthcare player in eastern India to construct a multispeciality hospital. Meanwhile, the cables and conductors business received orders in both domestic and international markets.

Commenting on these wins, Kejriwal said the Oman order would further diversify the company's order book in the Middle East, while the hospital project would strengthen its presence in the healthcare construction segment.
Following these orders, the company's year-to-date order intake had crossed Rs.10,600 crore, according to the 23 October announcement.

KEC International reported a 41% year-on-year decline in net profit to Rs.73 crore in the April-June quarter of FY27, compared with Rs.125 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, the company said in a statement.
Revenue remained largely unchanged at Rs.5,024 crore in the reporting quarter, against Rs.5,023 crore in the year-ago period.
The company's year-to-date order intake stood at Rs.6,303 crore across its transmission and distribution, civil, renewables, cables and conductors, and transportation businesses.
Meanwhile, KEC International reduced its net debt by more than Rs.150 crore to Rs.6,568 crore as of 30 June, reflecting an improvement in its debt position.
KEC International share price closed 1.25% down at Rs.327.55 apiece on the BSE.

KEC International shares have remained under significant selling pressure, with the stock declining 6.99% over the past week and 11.40% over the past two weeks. The correction has deepened over longer periods, with the stock falling 18.59% in one month, 30.71% over three months and 43.54% over six months.
The stock has declined around 55.65% year-to-date, reflecting sustained weakness in its share price.
